sources.fact: Duke Health, 'Contagious Yawning May Not Be Linked to Empathy; Still Largely Unexplained' (2014): 328 healthy volunteers watched a three-minute video of people yawning; 222 contagiously yawned at least once; as age increased participants were less likely to yawn, but age explained only 8 percent of the variability; no association between contagious yawning and empathy; contagious yawning can be triggered by hearing, seeing or thinking about yawning

Bartholomew & Cirulli, PLoS ONE 2014, 'Individual Variation in Contagious Yawning Susceptibility Is Highly Stable and Largely Unexplained by Empathy or Other Known Factors': 328 participants, 3-minute video; 222 (67.7%) yawned at least once; age explained only 8% of variability; no influence of empathy once age is accounted for; contagious yawning can be triggered by hearing, seeing, reading, or thinking about yawning
University of Washington, Neuroscience for Kids, 'Contagious Yawning': reading about yawning and thinking about yawning are listed as triggers

post.instagram_caption:
Just reading about a yawn can make you yawn 🥱

Contagious yawns can be set off by seeing, hearing, reading or even thinking about a yawn. In a Duke study, 328 people watched a 3 minute yawning video and about 68% yawned at least once. The study found no clear link to empathy, and age explained only about 8% of who yawned.

The rest is still a mystery.

Sources: Duke Health, PLoS ONE, University of Washington.
